text:
nina_finance: Heads-up for teams — policy change rolling out 15 May: were enforcing monthly spend caps on any SaaS billed to company cards or virtual cards that exceed $1,000/month (annualized ~$12k). The goal is fewer surprise invoices and better alignment with reserved capacity budgeting. See the short guide: https://redwood.app/finance/spend-caps :page_with_curl:
raj_ops: Quick Q — does this affect existing virtual cards issued by procurement? We have a few cards for infra tooling that spike during onboarding.
kevin_prod: Also — curious about reimbursements for customer-reimbursable tooling. We sometimes buy a license on card then invoice the customer.
nina_finance: Answers: 1) Virtual cards issued by procurement will be subject to the cap if the monthlyized spend exceeds the threshold. 2) Customer-reimbursable purchases should still go through expense reports; add the `#reimbursable` tag in the portal and attach the customer PO. Procurement will not block reimbursements but will flag items that exceed caps for review.
procure-bot: New rule added: `CardRules > MonthlyCap > 1000` (auto-flag). If an item is flagged, procurement will attempt auto-mitigation (issue temporary hold and notify owner).
olivia_legal: Reminder: any purchase with termination fees, indemnity changes, or data-processing attachments must route to legal before approval — that part is unchanged. If unsure, mark "requires legal" in the portal at submit time.
raj_ops: Is there an exception flow for urgent operational purchases (e.g., outage mitigation) where waiting for review would hurt customers?
nina_finance: Yes  emergency exception path exists. Use the portal button `Request Emergency Purchase` and include a short justification. Procurement will escalate to a delegated approver within 2 hours during business hours. Outside business hours, use the oncall procurement escalation list (procure-oncall@redwood.com). We log all emergency approvals for postmortem.
kevin_prod: Are we piloting delegated approvers? For large teams we sometimes need local approvers to avoid bottlenecks.
nina_finance: We're piloting delegated approvers for three teams (Infra, Growth, Platform). Delegated approvers can approve up to $5k/month per vendor for their team. To request delegation, team leads should submit a form (Procure > Controls > Delegation) and include approver's manager sign-off. The pilot details are in the guide.
procure-bot: Reminder: missing metadata (#project, #cost-center, owner) will cause auto-flag and delay. Auto-flagged items will show under `Procurement > Action Required` in the portal.
raj_ops: What auditing will happen after rollout? Would be good to know if we'll get contacted for cleanup.
nina_finance: Procurement will run a 30-day audit of new caps and emergency exceptions. Teams may receive quick follow-ups asking for receipts, owner confirmation, or growth estimates. We'll share a short findings dashboard at the end of the audit window.
kevin_prod: Thanks. Can you post a 3-line checklist we can paste into our team runbooks?
nina_finance: Posted in the guide. TL;DR: 1) Submit purchase in portal 2) Add #project, #cost-center, owner, and expected monthly run rate 3) If urgent, use `Request Emergency Purchase`. If in doubt, choose `pre-approval`.
olivia_legal: Minor addendum: contractors vs vendors — ensure contractor subscriptions are tied to a vendor record (Procurement > Vendors) and include SOW or invoice terms.
raj_ops: Good — we'll start updating our vendor owners this week. Thanks for the heads-up.
nina_finance: Thanks everyone. Well monitor first 30 days and tweak thresholds if needed. Ping me or open a procurement ticket for edge cases. :eyes:
